correctness.rationale: From the actual RESULT.md summing the x-variable gives K_q(a,b,c)=q^-2 sum_{y:a+c*y^3=0} psi(b*y), with correct q^-3 Fourier inversion. The sharp operator norm is the l1 kernel mass by finite convolution phase alignment. For c=0 only the origin q^-1 persists; c≠0,a=0 gives q(q−1) singleton coefficients q^-2; c,a≠0 gives one root if d=1, otherwise (q−1)^2/3 pairs each with a three-root orbit. Three p-th roots of unity cannot sum zero for p≠3 because exact equilateral cancellation requires primitive third roots and d=3 excludes characteristic3. This proves support counts and the norm formula and full multiset. Trace surjectivity gives a 1D prime-field phase when ζ∈F_p (p≡1 mod3) or rank-two joint phase when p≡2 mod3 with even extension degree; the determinant of the linear change is 3, invertible. In the p≡1 branch Fourier-character tests show one-dimensional slopes ζ_p yield equidistribution on T²: any fixed (k,l) relation would force p to divide fixed positive k²+k*l+l². Riemann sums then yield the established random-walk mean C_3. The claimed unitary Fourier ratio equals sqrt(q) times the projection norm by Parseval and |S_q|=q². Fresh independent direct double Fourier sums across ALL q³ frequencies for prime q=3,5,7,13 agreed with exact root expressions, sharp norms and nonzero coefficient counts; prime fields alone do not certify extension-field rank, handled by trace linear algebra.
